user.title: Add a Telegraf receiver
user.description: Creates a local-only webhook that Telegraf's `outputs.http` plugin can send metrics to. Sensors are created automatically as metrics arrive.

data_description.name: Shown as the integration entry title, e.g. the Telegraf instance it receives from.

create_entry.default:
Webhook URL (reachable from your local network only):

`{webhook_url}`

Add this to your Telegraf configuration and restart Telegraf:

```toml
{telegraf_config}
```

Only a few core sensors (CPU, memory, swap, load, boot time, temperatures) are enabled automatically. Everything else Telegraf sends, including disks and network interfaces, is added **disabled**: enable what you want on the device page, or in bulk under Settings → Entities.

**Tip:** if you use `[[inputs.sensors]]` (lm-sensors), choose `remove_numbers` (default `true` gives `fan_input`, `false` gives `fan1_input`) before sending data and keep it. Both styles get correct units, but the field name is part of each sensor's identity: changing the setting later creates new sensors and leaves the old ones unavailable.

You can see the URL again in the integration's options.

data.local_only: Only accept requests from the local network

data_description.include_measurements: Only create sensors for measurements matching one of these glob patterns (e.g. `cpu`, `disk*`). Leave empty to include all. Existing sensors that no longer match are removed.
data_description.exclude_measurements: Never create sensors for measurements matching these glob patterns. Takes precedence over includes; existing sensors that now match are removed.
data_description.stale_timeout: Mark a sensor unavailable if no value arrived for this many seconds. Keep it above your longest Telegraf collection interval. 0 = never.
data_description.connectivity_timeout: Turn a host's Connectivity off if it sent nothing at all for this many seconds. 0 = never.
data_description.max_entities: Safety limit for automatically created entities. Each host's Connectivity counts too, so a new host needs room for two.
data_description.local_only: Uses Home Assistant's local-network check, which only accepts private addresses (e.g. `192.168.x.x`, `fdxx::`). Turn this off if Telegraf reaches Home Assistant over global IPv6 addresses and the log shows `Received remote request for local webhook`. Requests through Home Assistant Cloud (Nabu Casa) are always rejected, but when this is off, anyone who can reach Home Assistant directly and knows the webhook URL can send metrics.

entity_cap_reached.title: Telegraf entity limit reached
entity_cap_reached.description:
The Telegraf entry **{title}** reached its limit of {max_entities} entities, so new metrics are ignored and no new sensors are created.

Raise **Maximum number of entities** in the integration's options, or filter the metrics Telegraf sends (e.g. with `namepass`/`fieldinclude` or the integration's include/exclude measurements). Changing the options reloads the entry and clears this issue.
